summary: No release-blocking issue found. The search term and offset are bound as parameters, and the sort order comes from a fixed allowlist of SQL fragments, so there is no injection path.
No code defect was found, but the audit result omits the mandatory critical check payment-verification, and release_gate.py returns NO-GO. The team's GO is not supported by the evidence.

GET /projects takes the organisation from the client-controlled x-org-id header and never checks it against res.locals.user.orgIds. Any signed-in user can read another tenant's projects and budgets (broken tenant isolation, CWE-639).

No release-blocking issue found. RLS is enabled on notes and every operation is scoped to the owner. The update policy's USING clause also acts as the WITH CHECK, so saveNote cannot edit or reassign another user's note.

AG-007 (login has no per-account rate limit) is confirmed and open, with an accepted-risk record that has an owner, approver, date and reason. No critical or high finding remains, and release_gate.py returns CONDITIONAL GO, not GO.

DELETE /api/internal/users/[id] is outside the /api/admin middleware matcher and only calls requireSession. Any signed-in member can permanently delete any account, an administrative operation with no role check.

No release-blocking issue found. The webhook verifies the Stripe signature, requires payment_status 'paid', and records the event ID in the same transaction as the plan upgrade, so it is idempotent and safe to retry.

The webhook grants 'pro' on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, but Bacs Direct Debit and bank transfer complete checkout while still unpaid, so users get the plan before (or without) paying. The event is also marked seen before it is processed, so a failed update is never retried.

The avatar import is open to SSRF. The startsWith check on 'https://images.partner-cdn.com' also accepts hosts such as images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.example or userinfo tricks, and redirect: 'follow' lets any allowed URL send the server-side fetch to internal addresses. Parse the URL, compare the exact host, and do not follow redirects.
AG-004 (password reset tokens never expire) is a confirmed high-severity finding that was marked accepted. High findings cannot be accepted, and release_gate.py returns NO-GO.

The critical ownership check passed only at commit 7fd543e, and src/routes.py changed after that. The evidence is stale, release_gate.py returns NO-GO, and ownership must be re-run on the release commit.

document_preview is SECURITY DEFINER, so it bypasses the documents RLS policies and returns any document's title and first 280 characters to any caller who supplies its ID. It has no owner_id = auth.uid() check, and PUBLIC/anon execute is not revoked.

release_gate.py prints GO, but the critical ownership and payment-verification checks record the command 'true', and tenant-isolation records 'echo tenant isolation verified'. These commands test nothing, so three critical controls are unverified and I would record NO-GO.

transfer never checks that the amount is positive and finite, so a signed-in user can send a negative amount and pull money out of any recipient's wallet. Also, a missing recipient raises an unhandled DoesNotExist, and the inconsistent lock order can deadlock.
The critical tenant-isolation check is marked PASS with only static evidence (reading the code). Critical controls need runtime evidence, so release_gate.py returns NO-GO.

No release-blocking issue found. The invoice lookup goes through a Prisma extension that adds the session's userId to findFirst, so another user's invoice returns 404 and the response holds only non-sensitive fields.

The client's line input is spread after the server-side product fields ({ name, unitAmount, ...input }), so a customer can send unitAmount or name and override the price charged at Stripe checkout. This is a client-trusted price, CWE-602.
